issues.title: Incorrect normalization in the condition-number gradient
issues.failure_explanation: In the smooth singleton-eigenvalue regime, lem:optkappacond gives each eigenvalue gradient as (lambda_i/(x_i^TDx_i))(x_i bullet x_i). The quotient rule therefore requires the first term of the condition-number gradient to use x_1^TDx_1. The old statement divides the x_1 term by x_n^TDx_n, contrary to its proof and in a manner that changes under independent rescaling of x_1.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed gradient is wrong for general d. The optimality characterization at d=e is unaffected because normalized extreme eigenvectors then have equal denominators, and later direction formulas already use the two correct normalizations.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the smooth singleton-eigenvalue formula in thm:optcondkappa, replace the denominator of the first term by x_1^T D x_1, so that the gradient is κ(d)[(x_1 bullet x_1)/(x_1^T D x_1) − (x_n bullet x_n)/(x_n^T D x_n)]. No proof or downstream change is needed.
issues.why_classification: The preceding eigenvalue-gradient lemma and the theorem's own quotient-rule calculation already contain the uniquely correct normalization. The displayed use of x_n^T D x_n in both terms is therefore transcriptional; correcting it repairs no inference and preserves all guarantees.

issues.title: Raw objective values incorrectly claimed to decrease monotonically

diagnostic_evidence.quote: since \Cref{GD} is a subgradient method, in general it is not a descent method.

issues.failure_explanation: For the GD iterates under the stated diminishing, nonsummable stepsizes, the old theorem claims that the raw sequence kappa(cDo(d_k)) decreases monotonically to kappa_*. The argument establishes only that its liminf is kappa_*, which neither implies monotonicity nor even full convergence of the raw sequence. The old paper also says the method is not generally a descent method. By contrast, the defined running best value kappa_*^j is nonincreasing by construction and converges to kappa_* once the liminf conclusion holds.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem overstates convergence of the actual objective sequence. Its liminf guarantee remains intact, and the correct monotone guarantee applies only to the running best values.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the established statement liminf_{k→∞} κ(cDo(d_k)) = κ_*. Define the running best value κ_*^k = min_{1≤j≤k} κ(cDo(d_j)) and replace the false raw-sequence conclusion by κ_*^k decreasing monotonically to κ_*. Make no claim that the raw objective values are monotone or converge as a full sequence.
issues.why_classification: A non-descent subgradient method and a liminf result do not support monotonicity or full convergence of the raw objective sequence. Replacing that promise by running-best convergence is a meaningful but limited weakening, so it is not a typo or same-guarantee minor repair. The replacement follows immediately from the retained liminf result, requires no new proof architecture, and preserves a comparable optimal-value convergence guarantee.

issues.title: Ill-typed block dimensions in the optimal scaling proposition
issues.failure_explanation: The proposition partitions the n columns of M into blocks of widths n_i, with sum n. A right block-diagonal multiplier must consequently have square n_i-by-n_i blocks. Under the old declaration, blkdiag(B_i) has km rows and n columns, so the product M times that matrix is generally nonconformable. Independently, (M_i^TM_i)^{-1/2} is necessarily n_i-by-n_i, contradicting the declared m-by-n_i type.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition's optimization problem and right-scaling construction are not well-typed for general admissible m and block sizes. The following block-preconditioning corollaries rely on the corrected square-block formulation; the last corollary also has the separate factor-orientation defect adjudicated under C05.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the declared block type in prop:blckdiaf from B_i in R^{m×n_i} to B_i in R^{n_i×n_i}. Then blkdiag(B_1,…,B_k) is an n×n right multiplier, the product with M is conformable, and B_i=(M_i^T M_i)^{-1/2} has the declared type. Carry this square-block typing through the two listed corollaries without changing their dimension-related claims or proofs.
issues.why_classification: The old source itself uniquely forces square n_i-by-n_i blocks: the preceding definition calls them positive-definite blocks of order n_i, the displayed optimizer has that size, and the first dependent corollary already uses it. The erroneous m-by-n_i declaration is an ill-typed transcription on which the mathematical reasoning does not depend.

issues.title: Inverse-transpose Cholesky block fails to whiten the right scaling
issues.failure_explanation: Even under the favorable intended reading A_i=R_i^TR_i, the old factor is false. With one block, R=[[1,1],[0,1]], A=R^TR, and B=R^{-T}, one obtains B^TAB=[[1,-1],[-1,2]], whose omega value is 3/2. Taking B=R^{-1} instead gives B^TAB=I and omega=1. Thus R^{-T} is not generally optimal for the stated right-scaled objective, whereas R^{-1} has the required orientation.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary identifies the wrong triangular partial-Cholesky right factor and can yield a strictly suboptimal condition measure. Its 1-by-1 Jacobi observation and the preceding symmetric inverse-square-root block result are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For each block Cholesky factorization A_i=R_i^T R_i, replace the proposed right factor B_i=R_i^{-T} by B_i=R_i^{-1}. Replace the faulty orientation argument with the direct verification B_i^T A_i B_i=I, equivalently B_i B_i^T=A_i^{-1}, which places this factor within the optimal block-scaling family established by the preceding result.
issues.why_classification: The inverse-transpose factor and its supporting orientation argument are mathematically false, so this is not merely a transcriptional typo. Nevertheless, the correction is a short, standard Cholesky calculation, needs no new lemma or proof architecture, and preserves the exact optimal right-block preconditioning guarantee, with the Jacobi and inverse-square-root results unchanged.
